title: *Background analysis of climate risks to Syria's electricity and urban water sectors* (ODI: Think change1)
temporal_coverage: Historical trends to reconstruction scenarios through 2045+
methodology: New climate-trend analysis, population scenarios, water systems and electricity-demand analysis
limitations: Reconstruction-oriented; population scenarios are planning tools rather than forecasts; substantial data gaps acknowledged.

title: *Human-induced climate change compounded by socio-economic water stressors increased severity of drought in Syria, Iraq and Iran* (World Weather Attribution7)
geographic_coverage: Euphrates-Tigris basin including large parts of Syria and Iraq; Iran separately
methodology: 36-month SPEI; observations and climate models using published peer-reviewed attribution methods
limitations: Regional basin result cannot be generalized to every Syrian locality; rapid attribution study, not a conflict-causality study.

title: *Syrian Arab Republic Nationally Determined Contribution. NDC1* (Climate Laws8)
organization: Syrian Arab Republic / UNFCCC; mirror by Climate Change Laws of the World
methodology: Government NDC; repository metadata and topic extraction
limitations: Official UNFCCC primary PDF could not be fetched because of a redirect loop; repository topic extraction is explicitly beta. Detailed primary-text locator LOCATOR NOT VERIFIED.

title: *FAO GIEWS Country Brief - Syrian Arab Republic* (FAOHome2)
methodology: Crop, rainfall, input, import and food-security monitoring
limitations: Current operational synthesis rather than causal impact evaluation; subnational detail uneven.

title: *UNHCR Syria Operational Update - March 2026* (UNHCR Data Portal3)
methodology: Operational displacement, return and assistance data
limitations: Rapidly changing population movements; estimates depend on operational data systems.

title: *Syria at a turning point: A new chapter for children - Annual Report 2025* (UNICEF9)
geographic_coverage: All 14 governorates, with selected subnational examples
methodology: Programme monitoring and sectoral operational statistics
limitations: UNICEF self-report; beneficiary/reach numbers are outputs unless an evaluation establishes outcomes.

title: *The Syrian Conflict: Physical Damage and Reconstruction Assessment (2011-2024)* (World Bank4)
methodology: Predominantly remote data and asset/exposure modelling
limitations: Does not measure full human/economic impacts or service-restoration needs; remote-data uncertainty; sectoral disaggregation limited.

title: *Syria Common Country Analysis: 2024 Update* (UN Syria10)
methodology: Synthesis of UN, government and external evidence
limitations: Some environmental material derives from older sources; broad synthesis claims need source-level checking before causal use.

title: Kelley et al., *Climate change in the Fertile Crescent and implications of the recent Syrian drought* (Columbia OCP5)
temporal_coverage: Pre-2011 drought and longer climatic record
methodology: Observations, CMIP5 simulations and secondary social evidence
limitations: Historical and heavily contested causal interpretation; migration/conflict evidence relies partly on secondary sources.

title: Selby et al., *Climate change and the Syrian civil war revisited* (Cambridge Repository11)
methodology: Systematic interrogation of climate, migration and conflict evidence
limitations: Historical critique rather than evidence about current Climate-FCV mechanisms; cannot prove a zero climate effect.

title: Eklund et al., *Societal drought vulnerability and the Syrian climate-conflict nexus are better explained by agriculture than meteorology* (Nature12)
limitations: Cropland is not equivalent to household livelihood, migration or political behaviour; historical focus.

title: *Making Adaptation Work: Addressing the compounding impacts of climate change, environmental degradation and conflict in the Near and Middle East* (ICRC6)
geographic_coverage: Near/Middle East; examples from Syria, Iraq, Yemen
limitations: Many findings are regional rather than Syria-specific; not an impact evaluation.

title: *Syrian Arab Republic Interim Country Strategic Plan Evaluation 2018-25* (World Food Programme13)
limitations: Page publication date conflicts with stated evaluation period; downloaded evaluation PDF was not fetchable in this session; findings on publication page were verified. Not a climate-specific impact evaluation.

title: *JP Syria 2.0 Annual Programme Narrative Progress Report 2025* (MPTF Gateway14)
organization: UN Joint Programme: FAO, UNDP, UNFPA, UN-Habitat, UNICEF, WFP
methodology: Implementing-agency monitoring, lessons and reported outputs
limitations: Self-reported programme evidence, geographically narrow; lessons should not be treated as independently demonstrated outcomes.

title: *Increasing the climate change resilience of communities in Eastern Ghouta...* (Adaptation Fund15)
methodology: Project design, administrative and performance documentation
limitations: Project objectives and budgets are intended mechanisms, not proof of resilience outcomes; local evidence only.

title: *Approval of request for no-cost extension of project completion date: UN-Habitat (Syria)* (Adaptation Fund16)
methodology: Secretariat review of documented implementation delays
limitations: Establishes implementation delay and reported causes, not the magnitude of resulting resilience loss.

title: *Syria - Country Overview* (World Bank17)
methodology: World Bank synthesis and high-frequency indicators
limitations: Page explicitly notes limited and unevenly reliable official data; current estimates remain uncertain.
